section: § Graphene and a concrete Chern witness (Fig. 3)
finding: Both the figure title ('mass inversion is necessary, not sufficient, at fixed N') and the LaTeX caption ('necessary but not sufficient at fixed grid size') assert the NECESSITY direction. The 'not sufficient' half is kernel-certified (haldane_massInversion_not_sufficient_at_N4: m = 5 inside the window, C = 0). Necessity is not: no Lean theorem quantifies over m, and the certified support is the single sample m = 6 outside the window (haldane_trivial_phase_chern_zero). The claim is true (the N = 4 window 3.3177 is a strict subset of 3√3) but is prose-level, matching HaldaneWitness.lean's module header rather than a theorem. NOTE: the figure does NOT resurrect the retracted 'exactly where the masses invert' framing — that check passes.
recommendation: Hedge the necessity direction in both the figure title and the caption, e.g. 'not sufficient at fixed N (certified at m = 5); the necessary direction is sampled at m = 6, not proven for all m.'

finding: Unhedged universal negative over ALL proof assistants in two places. Abstract (l.44-47): 'infrastructure which, as we document, no proof assistant currently has.' Introduction (l.64-65): 'That route is not merely unformalized in current proof assistants; it is structurally unavailable.' The paper's own Sec.8 states the same class of claim correctly hedged ('To our knowledge, no proof assistant defines...') and concedes carve-out C2, that Cubical Agda has formalized the Gysin sequence and H*(CP^inf) -- 'precisely the substrate from which Chern classes are defined'. papers/D11/prior_art_novelty.md Sec.5(1) records that the Isabelle AFP was NOT directly searchable, so a universal negative over provers cannot be established, only made probable. Violates the project standing rule stated in that same file's preamble: 'Unhedged "first in any prover" language is a Stage-13 finding, not a stylistic preference' -- with a live sibling precedent (Phase 6BD's novelty refuted by QBlue, Rocq, arXiv:2509.18583). NOTE: the Mathlib-scoped half of the structural claim IS verified -- direct grep of the pinned checkout 81a5d257 confirms zero characteristic classes, zero de Rham cohomology, zero manifold form-integration, and all 14 'Chern' strings are 'Chernoff'.
recommendation: Insert 'to our knowledge' in both sentences and, in the abstract, scope the claim to Mathlib or point at Sec.8's carve-outs. Sec.5's route-disclosure sentence ('two-scale convergence is, to our knowledge, formalized in no proof assistant') is already the correct model to copy.

finding: Class IA substrate-count drift, Sec.1 'Substrate summary' (l.94-95): the paper states '6178 lines, 395 theorems and lemmas, 85 definitions and structures, counted at source level'. Recomputed at source level over the same 22 modules: LINES 6024 (wc -l; 6046 if a final partial line is counted per file) -> delta 2.56%; THEOREMS+LEMMAS 392 (334 theorem + 58 lemma) -> delta 0.77%; DEFS+STRUCTURES 83 (75 def + 6 structure + 2 abbrev; 0 instance, 0 inductive) or 81 counting def+structure strictly -> delta 2.4-4.9%. All three exceed the 0.5% tolerance and all three err HIGH. Alternative conventions tried and rejected: column-0-only theorem regex gives 379; a comment-tolerant substring match gives 412; neither reproduces 395. No 23rd D11 module explains the surplus (the tree was scanned for a module of ~154 lines / 3 theorems / 2 defs; no D11-plausible candidate exists). Not a staleness artifact: the 22 modules were last modified 2026-07-30 14:50, before the 21:53 lift. The MODULE COUNT (22) is correct and independently confirmed against lean_deps.json and docs/ARCHITECTURE_SCOPE.md:279. recommendation: Regenerate the three figures with an explicit one-line command and pin that command in the paper footnote or in papers/D11/change_log.md so the numbers are reproducible by a referee. Suggested source-level convention: theorems = lines matching ^\s*(@[...])*(private|protected|nonrec|noncomputable)*(theorem|lemma)\s; defs = same with (def|structure|abbrev); lines = wc -l.

finding: Sec.2 (l.155-157) attributes a biconditional to a one-directional lemma: '...and blochPauli_gap_pos (gapped if and only if the d-vector is nonzero)'. The declaration at lean/SKEFTHawking/BlochBundle.lean:95 is `lemma blochPauli_gap_pos (d : Fin 3 -> R) (hd : d != 0) : 0 < Real.sqrt (dNormSq d)` -- a single implication, with no converse shipped anywhere in the bundle. This is not Class TN (the name resolves) and not Class HD (no tracked hypothesis); it is a strength-attribution defect: the paper credits a named declaration with a logical form it does not have. It matters because the paper is otherwise scrupulous here -- Sec.4 explicitly flags pt_symmetric_real_spectrum_iff as a 'sharp biconditional' and adds 'Both directions carry content' -- so a referee reading the Lean will notice the asymmetry. ROOT CAUSE IS UPSTREAM: BlochBundle.lean's own docstring headline already reads 'The model is gapped iff d != 0' / 'the bands are separated by the gap 2|d| > 0 **iff** d != 0', so the paper faithfully inherited a substrate docstring overclaim. The underlying mathematics (0 < |d| <=> d != 0 for a real 3-vector) is trivially true, so no physics claim is false.
recommendation: Either (a) weaken the paper prose to 'gapped whenever the d-vector is nonzero', or (b) ship the one-line converse and restate blochPauli_gap_pos as an iff. In BOTH cases also fix the BlochBundle.lean docstring in the same pass, otherwise the same overclaim will re-enter the next bundle that lifts this module.

finding: 'radical-free real and imaginary comparisons' is inaccurate as literally read: arg_cell_A's own side-condition is `Real.sqrt 3 * z.im < z.re`, and HaldaneWitness.lean:85 records that the m=1 / m=6 discharges reason about sqrt5, sqrt37, sqrt41, sqrt45, sqrt101. finding: add_vrect / add_hrect shapes composite ABOVE the data traces — Plotly shapes default to layer='above'; none of the eight add_vrect/add_hrect calls in the four D11 figure functions overrides it. Every marker and curve inside a shaded region is therefore alpha-blended with the shading. Confirmed arithmetically to the unit on all three colour channels: Fig 3 markers 0.8*(230,57,70) + 0.2*(46,134,171) = (193,72,90) measured; Fig 4 marker 0.86*carmine + 0.14*steel_blue = (204,68,84) predicted vs (203,67,84) measured; Fig 1 markers 0.8*carmine + 0.2*amber = (232,74,56), 543 px measured.
